text:
harper-marketing: Quick pre-press ask: before we attach bench numbers to the launch post, can runtime run the 'audit sweep' and confirm methodology + gating? Need to avoid any follow-up corrections from press.

lee-runtime: Sure. What does marketing want included in the audit pack vs the usual minipack?

harper-marketing: Two additions: 1) a short statistical note saying we ran 3 independent sweeps and report median p95, and 2) a clear gating flag if variance or noise is above our threshold so we do NOT publish. Also need the CSVs and one reproducible script the reporter can run.

anas-eng: For the gating threshold, propose: if p95 across sweeps has coefficient of variation (std/mean) > 0.08 (8%) mark as noisy and schedule a rerun. Also if int8 p95 differs from fp16 p95 by >12% label quantization as preliminary. Thoughts?

lee-runtime: Sounds reasonable. We'll implement: three micro-sweeps (N=300 each), independent process starts, batching OFF, 30 warmup. Compute p50/p95/p99 per sweep, then report median and CV for p95. If CV > 0.08 we mark gate=FAIL. We'll attach timings combined and per-sweep, plus traces (cold/steady) and the script.

demo-ops: For reproducible script, can you include a dockerized minimal harness? Reporters like one-step: docker run -e KEY=$KEY redwood/bench-minirun:stable --model rwd-demo-2b --payloads payloads.csv --runs 3

lee-runtime: Yes, will include run_harness.sh and a docker example. We'll also include exact kernel/driver/docker tags in provenance.txt.

harper-marketing: Good. Also include a one-sentence consumer-facing note: "We ran three independent micro-sweeps; numbers reported are medians; see artifacts for per-sweep detail." We'll craft final wording but need the raw metrics.

anas-eng: Minor ask from eng: include a column 'sequence_length' in timings.csv and a small histogram file counts.json (or counts.csv) so marketing can verify distribution.

lee-runtime: Will add sequence_length column and counts.csv with buckets <=64, 65-512, 513-2048. We'll seed payloads so distribution is 50/30/20 by count.

audit-bot: audit-checklist: runs=3, per-run N=300, warmup=30, batching=OFF, collect p50/p95/p99, tokens_per_sec, sequence_length column required, provenance.txt required, demo/run_local.sh required.

harper-marketing: Important editorial gate: if any single long payload run takes >2x median p95, we want a note and potential exclusion of that sample. Don't want one outlier skewing press phrasing.

lee-runtime: We'll compute per-payload p95 and flag outliers (>2x median). Outliers will be annotated in timings.csv and excluded from median calc if deemed environment noise (and we'll state that in provenance).

demo-ops: Also include a tiny 'how-to-interpret' blurb for reporters: what median vs mean means here, and a note on quantized labels. Keeps press from misreading variance.

harper-marketing: Perfect. ETA? We need artifacts for editorial review tomorrow morning.

lee-runtime: I'll kick the job now. micro-audit #22008 queued. ETA ~6h. If any gate fails, I'll ping immediately and include raw traces.

audit-bot: micro-audit job #22008 queued by lee-runtime. Logs: /audit/22008.

lee-runtime: Job completed. Artifacts uploaded: /audit/22008/artifacts.tar.gz (sha256: 1a2b3c4d...). Summary: median p95 = 172ms, p95 CV = 0.065 (PASS), int8 delta vs fp16 = +9% (labeled preliminary but within delta threshold). Outlier: one long payload run spike at 390ms (annotated).

harper-marketing: Awesome. Can you drop the artifacts link here and a one-line press-ready blurb we can copy?

lee-runtime: press_blurb.txt included in artifacts: "Measured on rwd-demo-2b (dedicated-gpu-5). Median p95 = 172 ms over 3x300-request sweeps; batching disabled; see artifacts for per-sweep detail and provenance." Link: /audit/22008/artifacts.tar.gz

harper-marketing: Thanks. If any follow-up editorial calls come in, we'll loop you in. Great job catching the spike. :clap:
